title: Understanding MSE Components
text: The Mean Squared Error (MSE) is composed of three parts: the squared bias, the variance, and the irreducible error. Each of these components contributes to the overall error.

title: Shape of the MSE Curve
text: The MSE curve is typically U-shaped because as model complexity increases, the bias decreases while the variance increases. The irreducible error remains constant.

title: Finding the Minimum of the MSE
text: The minimum of the MSE occurs where the sum of the squared bias, variance, and irreducible error is the smallest. This is typically at a moderate level of model complexity.

hintAnswer: The MSE is the sum of the squared model bias the model variance and the irreducible error; it is approximately U shaped and its minimum occurs at the minimum of that curve.
